text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- ELETROBRAS AND BNDES FIGHT OVER 26 BLN REAIS

Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) and federal electrical power holding Eletrobras are fighting over who will become the financing agent for the electricity sector once it is privatized. Eletrobras holds the function now and administered 26 billion reais worth of financing last year.

The Votorantim group, which is Brazil's third largest pulp and paper maker, but also has interests in metals and cement, plans to expand its pulp and paper operations by doubling investments in the business by 2000 and increasing production to 2,000 tonnes of pulp per day.
-- PUBLIC SECTOR DEFICIT RISES AGAIN IN MARCH
After falling four consecutive months the public sector deficit is on the rise again in March, climbing to 3.61 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from 3.46 percent of GDP in February.
Two deputies who resigned their posts following allegations that they took money for voting in favor of a bill allowing President Cardoso to run for a second term in office will be investigated.
-- BANERJ CAN BE PAID FOR IN PRIVATIZATION BONDS
Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj is due to be privatized June 20 at a base price of 300 million reais and can be paid for wholly in privatization bonds.
-- PEUGEOT TO BUILD CARS IN RESENDE
French carmaker Peugeot has decided to open a $600-million car factory in Resende, Rio de Janeiro state, which will come on line in 1999 and produce 70,000 vehicles per year.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
